'''Azat Fanisovich Miftakhov''' ({{langx|tt-Cyrl|Азат Фәнис улы Мифтахов|translit=Azat Fänis ulı Miftaxov}}, {{langx|ru|Азат Фанисович Мифтахов}}; born March 22, 1993) is a [[Tatars|Tatar]]-[[Russia]]n [[mathematician]], convicted for acts of [[hooliganism]] against the [[United Russia]] ruling party.

==Early life and education==
Miftakhov was born on 22 March 1993 in [[Nizhnekamsk]], in the [[Tatarstan|Republic of Tatarstan]], [[Russia]].<ref name=born>{{cite web |url=https://memohrc.org/ru/defendants/miftahov-azat-fanisovich|language=Russian|trans-title=Miftakhov Azat Fanisovich |title= Мифтахов Азат Фанисович |publisher= Human Rights Center|date=30 April 2005 |website=[[Memorial (society)|Memorial]]|access-date=20 January 2021}}</ref> He showed an interest in [[mathematics]] from an early age, while still in [[primary school]].<ref name=born/> In 2010, he participated in the All-Russian Mathematical Olympiad for school children.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://olympiads.mccme.ru/vmo/2010/final/prot11.htm|language=Russian|trans-title=XXXVI All-Russian Olympiad for School Students in Mathematics (The final stage)|title=XXXVI Всероссийская олимпиада школьников по математике (Заключительный этап) |publisher=Олимпиады для школьников [Olympiads for schoolchildren]|date=April 2010|website=|access-date=21 January 2021}}</ref>

==Mathematical work==
Miftakhov, in 2009, enrolled in the [[MSU Faculty of Mechanics and Mathematics|Faculty of Mechanics and Mathematics]] of [[Moscow State University]] and graduated from it in 2015. From 2015 he was a [[Postgraduate education|postgraduate]] student at the Department of Theory of Functions and Functional Analysis of Mechanics, working for his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] with Dr {{Interlanguage link|Vladimir Igorevich Bogachev|ru|3= Богачёв, Владимир Игоревич}}, MSU professor,<ref name=dr>{{cite web |url=http://www.mathnet.ru/eng/person8592|language=English|title=Bogachev, Vladimir Igorevich |publisher= [[Steklov Institute of Mathematics]]|date=2021 |website=|access-date=20 January 2021}}</ref> as his supervisor.<ref name=super>{{cite news |last=Boyko |first=Vsevolod  |date=8 February 2019|language=Russian|trans-title=MSU post-graduate student detained on bombing and pogrom charges in 'United Russia'. Who is he? |title=Аспиранта МГУ задержали по делам о бомбе и погроме в 'Единой России'. Кто он? |url=https://www.bbc.com/russian/features-47142088 |work=[[BBC Russian Service]] |access-date=20 January 2021}}</ref>

==Activism, arrests, and trial==
Miftakhov, a "self-described [[Anarchism|anarchist]],"<ref name=anar>{{cite news |last=Avilov|first=Alexander  |date=18 January 2021|title=Russia Jails Math Grad Student for Attack on Ruling Party|url=https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2021/01/18/russia-jails-math-grad-student-for-attack-on-ruling-party-a72563|work=[[The Moscow Times]]|agency=[[TASS|Russian News Agency]]|access-date=20 January 2021}}</ref> was arrested on 1 February 2019, after law enforcement officers searched his [[Dormitory|student's dorm]] room, and accused of building an "explosive device" that had been found a year earlier in a city near [[Moscow]], [[Balashikha]]. He subsequently claimed that, during interrogation, he was tortured by the police.<ref name=tort>{{cite news |date=14 October 2020|title=Miftakhov's case : The death of a secret witness marks the latest twist in the trial of a Russian graduate student and anarchist activist |url=https://meduza.io/en/feature/2020/10/14/miftakhov-s-case|work=[[Meduza (website)|Meduza]]|access-date=20 January 2021}}</ref> The [[Prosecutor|prosecution authorities]] twice ruled that there wasn't enough evidence to charge Miftakhov so he was released from [[Detention (imprisonment)|detention]] on 7 February.

The same day, he was arrested again and charged with attacking the ruling political party's office in Moscow. On the night of 31 January 2018, unidentified persons had broken a window at [[United Russia]]'s office on Onezhskaya Street, Moscow, and threw inside a [[smoke grenade]]. There were four people initially named as [[suspect]]s in the case: anarchist activists Elena Gorban and Alexey Kobaidze, who both pleaded guilty and were [[Recognizance|released on their own recognizance]]; anti-fascist activist Andrey Eykin; and anarchist Svyatoslav Rechkalov.<ref name=tort/> The investigation was suspended in September 2018 and resumed in February 2019, after the arrest of Miftakhov, with the accusations now being reclassified as about [[hooliganism]], which is punishable by up to seven years in prison. Miftakhov was arrested after a "[[secret witness]]" under the [[pseudonym]] "Petrov" came forward and claimed he saw the graduate student near the United Russia office.<ref name=tort/>

[[File:Supporters Azat Miftakhov.jpg|thumb|Hundreds gathered to support Azat Miftakhov anticipating Moscow's Golovinsky Court verdict in January 2021]]

In February 2020, the prosecutor's office issued an indictment against Elena Gorban, Andrey Eykin, and Azat Miftakhov. According to the [[indictment]], they belonged to an anarchist movement called "[[People's Self-Defense (Russia)|People's Self-Defense]]",<ref group=note>Not related to the Ukrainian [[Civil Movement "People's Self-Defense"]]</ref> which was, at the time, blamed for the 2018 terrorist attack on the [[Federal Security Service]] building in [[Arkhangelsk]]. Miftakhov denied any affiliation with the "People’s Self Defense" and pleaded not guilty of involvement in the attack on the United Russia office.<ref name=tort/>

The trial began in Moscow's [[Moscow City Court|Golovinsky District Court]] in October 2020. On the 13th, the presiding judge accepted as authentic a document that stated secret witness "Petrov" had died in January 2020. The prosecution called on another secret witness, carrying the pseudonym "Karaulny",<ref group=note>Russian for "[[Security guard|guard]]", "[[Picket (military)|sentry]]", "[[Watchkeeping|watchman]]"</ref> who testified, via [[Videotelephony|video link]], that Azat Miftakhov was not only a member of the People's Self-Defense but an active participant in the movement's activities, involved "in anarchist training activities," such as "combat training, knife fighting, and training" where participants "practiced techniques [to use] against police officers."<ref name=tort/>

On 18 January 2021, the court found Miftakhov guilty of hooliganism and sentenced him to six years in a [[penal colony]], as the prosecution had proposed,<ref name=guilty>{{cite news |date=14 October 2020|title=Russia Jails Math Grad Student for Attack on Ruling Party|url=https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2021/01/18/russia-jails-math-grad-student-for-attack-on-ruling-party-a72563|agency=[[TASS|Russian News Agency]]|work=[[The Moscow Times]]|access-date=20 January 2021}}</ref> while handing the two other defendants, Elana Gorban to four years of probation and Andrey Eykin to two years of probation, with four years and three years of [[suspended sentence]]s.<ref name=others>{{cite news |date=18 January 2021|title=Moscow court sentences grad student Azat Miftakhov to six years in prison |url=https://meduza.io/en/news/2021/01/18/moscow-court-sentences-grad-student-azat-miftakhov-to-six-years-in-prison|work=[[Meduza (website)|Meduza]]|access-date=20 January 2021}}</ref>

==Protests==
Following the court's decision, but also during the trial, numerous protests were addressed to the Russian authorities for Miftakhov's treatment, such as the [[open letter]] issued on by the [[Société mathématique de France]],<ref name=snf>{{cite web |url=https://smf.emath.fr/actualites-smf/180121-lettre-suite-annonce-verdict-azat-miftakhov|language=en, fr|trans-title=Azat Miftakhov verdict : Letter signed by the SMF President|title=Azat Miftakhov verdict : Lettre signée par le Président de la SMF|publisher=[[Société mathématique de France]]|date=19 January 2021 |website=|access-date=20 January 2021}}</ref> another from the [[Brazilian Mathematical Society]],<ref name=braz>{{cite web |url=https://www.sbm.org.br/noticias/manifestacao-a-favor-de-azat-miftakhov|language=Portuguese|trans-title=Manifestation in favor of Azat Miftakhov |title=Manifestação a favor de Azat Miftakhov|publisher= [[Brazilian Mathematical Society]]|date=30 December 2020 |website=|access-date=20 January 2021}}</ref> and others. An open letter signed by many Russian scientists circulated in Russia<ref name=doxa>{{cite web |url=https://doxajournal.ru/uni/mathfac|language=Russian|trans-title=Open letter in support of mathematician Azat Miftakhov|title=Открытое письмо в поддержку математика Азата Мифтахова|publisher= |date=2019 |website=Doxa (student journal)|access-date=20 January 2021}}</ref> and found its way in western academia.<ref name=nyu>{{cite web |url=https://cims.nyu.edu/~rodion/azat/azat-eng.pdf |title=An open letter in support of Azat Miftakhov, a mathematician|publisher= [[New York University]]|date=2019 |website=Doxa (student journal)|access-date=20 January 2021}}</ref> Approximately one hundred mathematicians from many countries signed a petition to boycott the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|2022 International Congress of Mathematicians]], then programmed to be held in [[Saint Petersburg]], for various reasons, among which is the "sharp rising" in Russia of "the number of human rights defenders, journalists and scientists in Russian prisons and penal colonies", including specifically Miftakhov.<ref name=boycott>{{cite web |url=http://www.icm2022boycott.org/|publisher=Boycott ICM 2022 in Russia website|title=Boycott ICM 2022 in Russia|date=2021|access-date=26 January 2021}}</ref> Over a hundred Russian mathematicians, working both in Russia and abroad, called on the International Mathematical Union to postpone the 2022 International Congress of Mathematicians until the end of Miftakhov's imprisonment.<ref>{{Cite web|date=8 December 2021|title=An open letter of Russian mathematicians to IMU Executive Committee regarding mathematician and political prisoner Azat Miftakhov|url=https://caseazatmiftakhov.org/2021/12/08/an-open-letter-of-russian-mathematicians-to-imu-executive-committee-regarding-mathematician-and-political-prisoner-azat-miftakhov/}}</ref>

== Honors ==
The Fondation Mathématique [[Jacques Hadamard]] (FMJH) and the Laboratoire de Mathématiques d’Orsay (LMO) announced on February 23, 2021, that Azat Miftakhov is a Laureate of their incoming international mobility program called "junior scientific visibility" which aims to fund a period of research studies of a young talented international PhD students under the direction of a mathematician belonging to a FMJH-affiliated laboratory.

Azat Miftakhov was then named an honorary student of [[Paris-Saclay University]] on 4 March 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.universite-paris-saclay.fr/ecoles-doctorales/mathematiques-hadamard-edmh|title=A.Miftakhov honorary student|date=2021|access-date=3 June 2021}}</ref>

An Azat Miftakhov Day was organized on 16 June 2021, by the Azat Miftakhov committee and sponsored by the French Mathematical Society ([[Société mathématique de France]], SMF).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://trv-science.ru/uploads/329N.pdf|page=5|title=Azat Miftakhov Day|date=2021|access-date=3 June 2021}}</ref>
